GuestNetworkExecGate::claim_release returns one opaque claim lifetime only from Open; from BootClosed or Recovering it registers a Notify waiter before unlocking and retries after wake without touching VM pending-EXEC state; from FailStop it returns None immediately; GuestNetworkExecClaim's Drop ends that lifetime under the same lock and wakes waiters. Private active-claim counter bookkeeping is not an independently observed outcome.

GuestNetworkExecSupervisor::open_after_boot performs only BootClosed -> Open, wakes waiters, and returns false from every other state; is_boot_closed is the read-only precondition check used immediately before fresh-process mutation and is never treated as a runtime health signal; begin_recovery performs only Open -> Recovering and returns true only for the winning transition; complete_attempt applies only while Recovering, updates the first-remaining component or transitions to Open and wakes waiters, and returns false after Open/FailStop so late work cannot overwrite either; recovery_progress returns a value snapshot only while Recovering and None in every other state; fail_stop atomically transitions BootClosed/Open/Recovering -> FailStop, returns the one request to send on its first call and None on every later call (first-request-wins, idempotent-send), and wakes waiters. (This enumeration of GuestNetworkExecSupervisor's surface is non-exhaustive -- see feature-delta.md for the complete method list.)

steps.description: Activate the native-metal walking skeleton under the final CH-v53-compatible contract. Provision installs protection, raises/read-backs the TAP, and Cloud Hypervisor attaches it by name before READY. At or before the exact mTLS success event, only request-correlated validated ARP replies and request-correlated zero-payload TCP resets may exist, with exact TCX counter/mark equality and zero guard-drop/marker/peer/physical escape. After the event, two checked-in VM workloads communicate by name through real overdrive serve + overdrive deploy <SPEC>; the exact same-node leg-B socket is TLS 1.3 kTLS TX/RX with same-inode bidirectional splice, remains loopback-only with zero physical/ordinary-forwarding egress, and confines plaintext to intentional leg-F/leg-S tuples. Activates S-ND295-01.
criteria: The callee VM Service reports Running with replicas 1/1 and the caller VM Job reports success dependent on receiving the callee's reply, driven entirely through the real overdrive serve + overdrive deploy <SPEC> production entry points -- no test-only wiring installs a rule, binds a socket, programs a map, or supplies an address that production does not install/bind/program/supply itself.

Cloud Hypervisor v53 named-TAP behavior is treated as a fixed external contract: HostGuestNetworkProvisioner completes exact TAP-up/protection read-back before VMM start, and CloudHypervisorVmm continues to render only `--net tap=...,mac=...`. Native run f1a15668 is retained as negative evidence that a down TAP fails before READY at CH's mandatory SIOCSIFFLAGS/EPERM. No GuestNetworkProvisioner::activate, activation state/error, fd-bearing attachment, inherited descriptor, CH CAP_NET_ADMIN grant, delayed hotplug, confinement change, or new VMM method is added.

The exact timing receipt is the existing synchronous `mtls.intercept.install.success` event for the caller allocation, captured by a Layer installed before deploy. Exactly one event carries the exact allocation id; on_event samples CLOCK_REALTIME, the same domain as AF_PACKET SO_TIMESTAMPNS. Production source order remains awaited mtls_lifecycle.start_alloc with exact `2 + P` read-back -> event -> driver.release_for_exit_emission. The event is the intercept-live/workload-traffic barrier, not a zero-all-L2 claim; typed set polling remains semantic-only and kernel handles remain private receipts.

Every guest-originated caller-TAP frame with timestamp <= the event must have a present timestamp, exact caller TAP ifindex, PACKET_HOST or PACKET_OTHERHOST direction, untagged/nontruncated/non-ambiguous capture, registered guest source MAC, fixed bridge destination MAC, zero application markers, and one of exactly two forms: (1) Ethernet/IPv4 ARP reply with htype=1, ptype=0x0800, hlen=6, plen=4, opcode=2, guest SHA/SPA and bridge/gateway THA/TPA, correlated one-to-one to an earlier exact host ARP request; or (2) valid unfragmented guest-to-gateway TCP RST with zero payload, RST=1, SYN/FIN/PSH/URG=0, and reversed ports correlated to one earlier zero-payload host control segment. For an ACK-bearing trigger, the reset is `<SEQ=SEG.ACK><CTL=RST>`; otherwise `<SEQ=0><ACK=SEG.SEQ+SEG.LEN><CTL=RST,ACK>` per RFC 9293 §3.5.2. Trailing ARP padding is zero. Missing timestamp, uncorrelated/duplicate response, third EtherType/protocol/shape, IPv6, ICMP, UDP/DNS, ARP request/gratuitous reply, TCP payload/other flags/endpoints, or marker byte fails closed.

Read all eight typed TCX counters at capture-ready and immediately after the event under one stable node-shared program/map identity. Because counters are node-shared, loss-accounted capture is armed on every managed TAP in the two-workload example and any guest-originated non-caller-TAP frame in the bracket fails rather than being attributed to the caller. Checked deltas are exactly ArpPass = permitted caller ARP reply count and Intercept = permitted caller TCP reset count; GatewayHostPass, EndpointMapMiss, SourceMacSpoof, SourceIpArpSpoof, DirectBypassDrop, and MalformedDrop are zero. Existing semantic classifier evidence proves marks Accepted(0x295b) and Intercept(0x295a) plus TCP bridge-MAC rewrite. The exact D9 guard remains present and its DefaultDrop counter is unchanged. Loss-accounted peer-TAP/all-interface capture observes zero copies on another TAP or physical interface, zero direct caller-to-callee guest tuple, and zero pre-event application markers. Any counter/capture mismatch or loss fails.

The closed pre-event parser and request-response correlator are pure test helpers with exhaustive/table/property coverage for both accepted shapes and every rejected axis (timestamp, direction, interface, VLAN, truncation, source/destination identity, ARP fields/opcode/padding/correlation, IPv4 fragmentation/protocol, TCP flags/header length/payload/ports/sequence correlation, markers, unknown EtherType). Every source-local pure property carries the exact `/// CONTRACT_SHAPE: pure-function.` declaration; every transitioned native body carries `/// CONTRACT_SHAPE: bounded-change.` and names the full capture/counter/guard/event complement.

For this same-node peer, exactly one live `ss -H -n -t -i -e` leg-B record must run from the shared-bridge gateway address to the ServiceBackendsResolve-selected workload address and declared port and contain tcp-ulp-tls, TLS 1.3, txconf, rxconf, and one nonzero inode. /proc/self/fd must map that inode to exactly one in-process fd. After the first request/reply establishes steady state, the existing strace-style thread-group observation must show completed positive splice(2) with that exact fd as destination for the second request and source for its response, followed by the guest's byte-exact second reply. Zero/multiple tuple, inode, or fd matches, a missing splice direction, attribution to another fd, or ambiguous thread ownership fails closed. This exact kTLS state plus same-inode bidirectional splice is the same-node protected-transport proof; no product/test-hook API may be added.

One loss-accounted all-interface AF_PACKET capture (ifindex zero) starts before caller-VMM release and retains each frame's actual ifindex. The exact leg-B tuple and reverse must appear only on loopback and zero times on every non-loopback interface, proving the nft output divert/fwmark/table-100 local route prevented physical or ordinary-forwarding egress. On the shared bridge and managed TAPs, all four byte-distinct plaintext markers are permitted only on the caller guest-address-to-frontend leg-F tuple/reverse and exactly one non-kTLS leg-S tuple from node gateway address and ephemeral port to Service workload address and declared port, plus its reverse; both request/reply pairs must be present there, and direct caller-guest-to-Service-guest bypass must be absent. Every other observed non-loopback interface/tuple must contain zero markers. Capture drops/truncation, missing positive guest-local markers, sequence gaps/conflicts, leg-B on non-loopback, plaintext on an unapproved interface/tuple, or direct bypass fails closed. Native run e72385d6 proved same-node loopback AF_PACKET cannot supply complete TLS 0x17 records despite exact live kTLS, so loopback payload is not parsed as TLS; physical-wire 0x17 capture remains cross-host and outside #295.
